title: Buyers issued urgent warning about the purchase of honey in supermarkets
text:
With real honey prices around $ 3,000, or £ 2,370, for a worldwide ton, experts urge buyers not to be chopped when buying sweet things.
This is because the diluted honey costs around $ 500, or £ 400, per ton, is furtively pushing to the shelves of supermarkets with many who are not wiser.
The difference in the price is marked, however, it is not always easy for buyers to say whether they get 100 percent genuine honey in stores or not.
Certain honey marks combine EU honey with honey that is not from EU, a mixture that has existed for a while.
The latter may contain glucose syrup and other less expensive aggregate ingredients that are prohibited by EU regulations.
The syrups made with ingredients such as beets, rice or other cheap crops can be mixed to increase honey at low price.
However, these less expensive ingredients lack unique nutritional qualities and enzymes contained in real honey.
Get the genuine product: Not all honey contains exactly what you imagine
Last year, the evidence in charge of the Honey Authenticity Network and carried out by the Celvia de Estonia laboratory discovered that more than 90 percent of the honey bottles of the main British retailers were full of cheap fillings such as sugar syrups.
In total, 24 of the 25 retail honey jars were considered “suspects” as a result of laboratory tests.
On the contrary, the five samples of the local British beeketers passed the authenticity tests.
Speaking to this this money, Dale Gibson, from Bermondsey Street Bees, said: ‘The availability of false honey at the prices of 80 percent below the real cost of production has tempted fungi, large commercial players, to drastically reduce your honey purchases. Authentic honey producers in the United Kingdom at token levels and filled with anonymous and adulterated “honey”.
“It is food fraud, simple and simple.”
He added: “Any honey that has been” mixed “has been industrially processed, treated with heat, killing essential enzymes, and obtained from nebulous origins and built by food scientists. That means avoiding anything labeled as” a mixture of … “
“The bees have already mixed the true nectar honey harvested from natural sources of trees, shrubs and flowers.”
Lynne Ingram, president of the Honey UK Honey Authenticity Network, said this is money: “Globally, honey prices have been reduced as the market is flooded with” honey “imported cheap.
‘In Great Britain we import 51,000 tons of honey, of which a growing percentage (77%) is from China (39,000) tons.
“These impossible low prices mean that genuine honey producers are being expelled from all over the world, since they cannot compete with the” honey “produced in factories. Anywhere in the world you can produce and sell real honey by 69p per bottle.
Carefully examine honey ingredients So, before buying a honey bottle in the supermarket, it is worth examining the list of ingredients.
When I first look at honey in stores, be sure to verify your origin carefully.
Mrs. Ingram said: ‘Buyers should buy British honey ideally. Read the label: I should say “it produces from the United Kingdom.” If the label says “produced in the United Kingdom”, that generally means that the content comes from abroad but is full in the United Kingdom.
“Be careful with” honey “saying” a mixture of honey that is not of EU “or” mixture of honey of many countries “, much of this will have come from China and it cannot be guaranteed that it is pure honey.”
She added: ‘Sometimes enzymes are added to honey diluted with syrups, to imitate natural enzymes added to honey by bees.
You can add ‘pollen, if the “honey” has leaked ultra or placed through resin technologies to eliminate antibiotics or pesticides, to replace what has been leaked.
The Real Deal: Dale Gibson directs Bermondsey Street Bees
“Sometimes things are eliminated from” honey. ”
‘For example, certain markers appear in tests that indicate that honey has been adulterated.
“Now we are seeing the Chinese honey factories that sell” RMN “Test” Honey “, designed to obtain round tests of honey authenticity.”
Sunna Van Kampen, founder of Tonic Health, said it is money: ‘The tests have shown that more than 90 percent of honey on supermarket shelves is not pure honey and has probably been cut with sugar syrup to be more affordable.
‘Most of the honey and even organic honey are often from a mixture of the EU and the EU honey, which means that there are many opportunities for honey to get out of the way.
“We always advise our community to seek honey of unique origin to limit the possibilities of adulteration in the supply chain.”
At present, in Great Britain there is no requirement to identify the countries of origin of honey mixed with more than one country.
According to Black Mountain Honey, if you place a tablespoon of real honey without diluting in a glass of water, you must settle at the bottom of the glass without dissolving quickly. If you dissolve quickly, it may not be the real business.
This week, the Food Standards Agency told The Independent that, although “there is no evidence that any honey for sale in the United Kingdom is insecure, it is a product that may be at risk of fraud.”
The EU has introduced new test methods and labeling laws to ensure that buyers can trust where their honey comes from and what it contains. However, Great Britain has not yet followed its example.
A spokesman for the Department of Environment, Food and Rural Affairs said this is money: ‘We take any type of food fraud very seriously.
‘There is no place for adulterated honey that undermines consumer confidence and the disadvantages of responsible companies acting within the law.
“We work in close collaboration with compliance authorities to ensure that honey sold in the United Kingdom is not subject to adulteration, meets our high standards and maintains a level game field among honey producers.”
On whether it is being done enough to stop the diluted honey that hits our shelves, Mr. Gibson of Bermondsey Street Bees said: ‘Honey regulations (England) 2015 are perfectly suitable for disqualifying false honey.
‘It is the political will and the absence of resolution according to food standards that are missing. Again and again, the results of the tests call adulterated supermarket honey, however, no compliance measures are taken.
‘Honey fraud is a great business, with gorce margins as fat as drug smuggling, but without the risk that the door of his room will collapse and a gun pointed to his head at 4 am
‘That is why Honey is the third most adult food on the planet, behind the wine and olive oil.
“That is what our bees and beekeepers face.”
Mrs. Ingram said: ‘The EU 2024 honey directive requires that all countries of origin in imported honey mixtures are listed in the labels in order of quantity.
‘We call on the United Kingdom government that aligns with this, so that consumers can make an informed decision about what they are buying.
‘A “mixture of honey that is not of EU” on the label means that the consumer has no idea where the product comes, what he is buying or putting in the mouth. The syrup does not have the health properties of real honey.
